context: Global average effective dose from natural sources (UNSCEAR 2000/2008): cosmic radiation + terrestrial gamma + radon + internal; range: 1-50 mSv/yr worldwide depending on location
chernobyl_comparison: Average European received ~1-2 mSv total Chernobyl lifetime dose = ~0.5-1 year equivalent natural background; average liquidator (117 mSv) = 49 years of global average background (or 5 years at higher local backgrounds)
source: UNSCEAR 2000 Sources and Effects; UNSCEAR 2008 Annex B; WHO Natural Background

context: Radon (Rn-222) from U-238 decay in soil and building materials; accumulates in poorly-ventilated basements and buildings; alpha emitter; irradiates bronchial epithelium; 52% of total natural background globally; major lung cancer cause (~21,000 deaths/yr USA from radon-induced lung cancer per EPA)
chernobyl_comparison: Radon dose dwarfs average Chernobyl public doses; most people live with 1.26 mSv/yr from radon alone; entire Chernobyl lifetime extra dose for most Europeans (~1-2 mSv) is less than one year of radon; shows importance of context when discussing Chernobyl doses
source: UNSCEAR 2000; EPA Radon Guide 2012; WHO Indoor Radon Handbook 2009

context: Cosmic rays: high-energy protons and nuclei from space; attenuated by atmosphere; at sea level: 0.39 mSv/yr effective dose; increases with altitude: at 3000m (Denver Colorado): ~0.8 mSv/yr; at 12000m (aircraft cruising): ~2-3 µSv/hr; astronauts: 1-3 mSv/day
chernobyl_comparison: Frequent flier receiving 200 hours/yr at high altitude: ~0.4-0.6 mSv/yr additional; comparable to some European Chernobyl doses; Denver Colorado residents receive 3x more cosmic radiation than coastal residents
source: UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B; ICRP 132 2016 Cosmic; FAA aviation dose

context: Gamma radiation from primordial radionuclides in soil: K-40 (most abundant); Th-232 series; U-238 series; varies by geology: granite regions higher (0.7-1.5 mSv/yr); limestone/sedimentary regions lower (0.1-0.3 mSv/yr); affected by building materials (granite stone higher)
chernobyl_comparison: Background external gamma component is the same pathway affected by Chernobyl Cs-137 deposition; liquidators received elevated external gamma primarily from soil contamination; 0.0043 µSv/hr per kBq/m² Cs-137 (see dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv)

context: Natural internal dose from consuming food and water: K-40 (dominant: 0.17 mSv/yr; 4400 Bq of K-40 in average human body); C-14 (0.012 mSv/yr); Pb-210 + Po-210 from seafood and smoking (~0.05-0.5 mSv/yr from Po-210 in seafood)
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl internal dose via food chain was significant in 1986 but is now orders of magnitude below K-40 natural internal dose; K-40 in human body: 4400 Bq vs typical post-1987 Cs-137 body burden <10 Bq/kg = <700 Bq total in adult = 6x less than K-40

context: Ramsar (northern Iran): Ra-226 enriched thermal spring water used in construction; some dwellings receive 260 mSv/yr (external dose); inhabitants have lived there for generations; extensive epidemiological studies show no confirmed cancer excess; used by hormesis advocates
chernobyl_comparison: Ramsar residents at 260 mSv/yr receive more dose in 1 year than Chernobyl liquidators received in lifetime; no confirmed cancer excess = contested evidence for threshold/hormesis; UNSCEAR notes Ramsar background studies have methodological limitations; small population size
source: Mortazavi SM 2002 Radiat Prot Dosimetry; UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B High Background; contested_radiation_science_REAL.csv

context: Guarapari Brazil thorium-rich monazite sands; beach dose rates 15-40 µSv/hr; beach visitors may receive several mSv in a day; local residents 50-100 mSv/yr from external gamma; also Kerala India and Yangjiang China monazite zones
chernobyl_comparison: Residents in these high background areas receive equivalent of Chernobyl liquidator doses (115 mSv) naturally within 1-2 years; no confirmed elevated cancer rates in multiple studies; another example supporting dose rate effects and threshold arguments
source: UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B; Morishima H 1997 J Radiat Res; IAEA High Natural Background

context: Airline crew receive elevated cosmic radiation; trans-Atlantic pilots: ~5 mSv/yr; some intercontinental routes (high latitude + high altitude): up to 9 mSv/yr; classified as radiation workers in EU; dose monitoring required above 1 mSv/yr
chernobyl_comparison: Airline crew receive doses comparable to lower range of Chernobyl liquidators; ~50-60% of European Chernobyl liquidators received <100 mSv (similar to what a 15-20 year airline career delivers); shows dose context for chronic occupational exposure
source: ICRP 132; EU BSS Directive 2013/59/Euratom; FAA 2008 Cosmic Radiation Report

context: Global average diagnostic medical radiation per person = 0.6 mSv/yr (UNSCEAR 2008); range: 0.03 mSv/yr in low-income countries to 2+ mSv/yr in high-income countries (US ~3 mSv/yr from medical imaging); single CT scan abdomen = 5-15 mSv
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl public doses (~1-2 mSv lifetime) comparable to 1-3 CT scans worth of dose; this is why UNSCEAR notes: most European Chernobyl doses are at levels already accepted in medical practice; important dose perspective context
source: UNSCEAR 2008 Annex A Medical; ICRP 105 2007; dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv

context: Denver Colorado (1600m elevation): ~0.8 mSv/yr extra cosmic vs sea level; typical Denver total background: 6-8 mSv/yr from radon (higher due to soil) + cosmic + terrestrial; compared to US average ~3 mSv/yr
chernobyl_comparison: Denver residents receive annual doses 2-3x higher than average American; over a 40-year lifetime: ~100-200 mSv extra vs sea-level US resident; no elevated cancer rate in Denver; frequently cited in LNT vs threshold debates
source: UNSCEAR 2000; NCRP Report 160 2009 US sources; NRC Background radiation

context: UNSCEAR 2008 projects average lifetime effective dose from Chernobyl for European population outside FSU: ~1-2 mSv per person from all pathways (ingestion + inhalation + external gamma); comparable to 0.5-1 extra years of natural background
chernobyl_comparison: Most Europeans received doses equivalent to 6-12 months of extra natural background from Chernobyl; far below threshold for any deterministic effects; LNT-based cancer projection involves extremely small individual risk multiplied across large populations
source: UNSCEAR 2008 Annex D para D604; nuclear_context_comparison_REAL.csv; unscear_population_doses_REAL.csv

context: In Belarus Ukraine Russia in 1986-1987: most contaminated populations received 5-50 mSv in first year (external + ingestion); some resettled populations: 10-200 mSv cumulative 1986-1990; contrast with evacuated 30km zone: evacuated April 27 (Prypyat) to later May (others) at 33-66 mSv/yr dose rates
chernobyl_comparison: 5-50 mSv additional dose in 1986-1987 for remaining population; still well below LD50 (3.5 Gy); below ARS threshold (0.7 Gy); within range of natural background in some geological areas; but significantly elevated vs their own pre-1986 background

context: K-40 (t1/2=1.248×10⁹ yr) natural radioisotope; 0.0117% of all potassium; human body maintains ~140g K → 4400 Bq K-40; cannot be reduced by diet (body regulates K homeostasis); emits beta and gamma; contributes ~0.165 mSv/yr internal dose
chernobyl_comparison: 4400 Bq K-40 in body vs average current Cs-137 in Ukrainian residents ~3 Bq/kg × 70 kg = ~210 Bq; K-40 is 20x more activity than Cs-137 in an average Ukrainian; shows that 'zero radiation' from food is physiologically impossible; K-40 is unavoidable
